Technical basis is correct: the 'exists' Lookup is keyed only on gen_customeraccount (or gen_policy in the pension flow), partial cache (CacheType=1) with NoMatchCachePercentage=0. The stated consequence 'two links will be created in the same run' is unconditional, but it holds only if (a) the account is covered by both operators (applypoa=1, or the employee is listed under each operator) and (b) the second row's Lookup executes before the first row's Create is committed. Rows in the same buffer are looked up before the asynchronous Union All hands them to the script; rows in different buffers may see the first link. The second sentence (a later run will not add a second operator) is correct.

wrongUnits.problem: Runtime consequence stated without the coverage and buffer-timing conditions.
wrongUnits.correct: If an employer has two valid operator POAs that both cover the employee, the same run can create two links for the account/policy. This happens when both rows are looked up before either link is created, which is typical when they fall in the same pipeline buffer. In later runs, no further operator is linked to an already-linked account/policy.

results.detail: Units 1-8 and 10 are correct. Unit 9 says 'only exceptions while building the record reach the ETL warning'. This is not what the code does. ExecuteBulk() for a full batch (count == 500) is called inside the try, so an exception thrown by ExecuteMultipleRequest is also caught and sent to ErrorBuffer, tagged with only the 500th record's GUID; and because entitiesList.Clear() is skipped, the list never reaches exactly 500 again. The final partial batch is flushed in Input0_ProcessInput outside any try, so an exception there fails the data flow and stops the Success chain (later flows do not run). In addition, ErrorBuffer.Message is wstr(100); a longer ex.Message + GUID text throws inside the catch and fails the component.
results.evidence: DTSX:10084 main.cs:118-138 (try incl. ExecuteBulk at 128-131), 139-164, 170-180; Error output Message wstr(100)

wrongUnits.problem: Misstates which failures reach the ETL warning.
wrongUnits.correct: Per-record faults returned inside the ExecuteMultiple response are ignored (ErrorBuffer lines commented out). An exception thrown by a full 500-record batch is caught and reported as one ETL warning carrying only the triggering row's GUID, if the message fits wstr(100); otherwise the component fails. An exception in the final partial-batch flush (outside the try) fails the data flow, and the following Success-chained flows do not run.
